texts: In an adult with a discrete coarctation at the isthmus, a gradient of 40 mmHg, hypertension, rib notching and collaterals, the best treatment is a transcatheter stent.
A stent holds the segment open and does better than balloon angioplasty alone, which in adults brings more recoil, restenosis and aortic wall injury.
Resection with end-to-end repair is the classic operation in children; in adults with suitable anatomy, stenting is less invasive and is the first choice.
Treating the hypertension alone leaves the obstruction and its long-term risks.
